sense: a school for study after school

terms.gloss: a college: of a university, or a school for older students
evidence: M-O s.v. department7: college (within a university)
M-O s.v. school types: university: college, after Tursellinus (1652)
terms.comment: Classically a body of colleagues, a board or guild: mercātōrum collēgium īnstituere (Liv. 2.27.5). The Jesuits called their schools collēgia, though these gave no degrees, and the colleges of Oxford and Cambridge are collēgia too (Morgan–Owens). An American college, which is a university, is ūniversitās studiōrum or acadēmīa (see university).

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. school types: university: college; department7: college.
